parts.zh: 一名服务员将一张价值近42.4万美元的支票归还给了遗失它的退休社工
W: 好的。您想了解什么?
M: 嗯,我邻居大概一年前在他屋顶上装了太阳能板
W: 嗯,我不了解您邻居的情况或他的具体配置
M: 好的,那听起来差不多
W: 先生,您有兴趣在您的屋顶上安装太阳能板吗?
W: 如果您愿意来我们办公室
W: 价格会因不同因素而有所变化

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the waiter?
options: He wanted to buy a home.
He suffered from a shock.
He lost a huge sum of money.
He did an unusual good deed.
optionsZh: 他想买房。
他遭受了震惊。
他损失了一大笔钱。
他做了一件不同寻常的好事。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：He did an unusual good deed.（他做了一件不同寻常的好事。）

questions.stem: What did the customer try to do when she got her check back?
options: Invite the waiter to a fancy dinner.
Tell her story to the Daily News.
Give some money to the waiter.
Pay the waiter's school tuition.
optionsZh: 邀请这位服务员去高档餐厅用餐。
把她的故事告诉《每日新闻》。
给这位服务员一些钱。
支付这位服务员的学费。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Give some money to the waiter.（给这位服务员一些钱。）

questions.stem: What is Maref's vote on Tuesday about?
options: Whether or not to move to the state's mainland.
How to keep the village from sinking into the sea.
Where to get the funds for rebuilding their village.
What to do about the rising level of the seawater.
optionsZh: 是否搬迁到该州的大陆。
如何防止村庄沉入海中。
从哪里获得重建村庄的资金。
如何应对海平面上升的问题。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Whether or not to move to the state's mainland.（是否搬迁到该州的大陆。）

questions.stem: Why did Donna Barr say they wouldn't see the plan carried out any time soon?
options: It takes too long a time.
It costs too much money.
It has to wait for the state's final approval.
It faces strong opposition from many villagers.
optionsZh: 需要太长时间。
花费太多资金。
必须等待州政府的最终批准。
面临许多村民的强烈反对。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：It costs too much money.（花费太多资金。）

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the social experiment?
options: To investigate whether people are grateful for help.
To see whether people hold doors open for strangers.
To explore ways of inducing gratitude in people.
To find out how people express gratitude.
optionsZh: 调查人们是否对帮助心存感激。
看人们是否会为陌生人扶门。
探索激发人们感恩之心的方法。
弄清人们如何表达感激之情。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：To investigate whether people are grateful for help.（调查人们是否对帮助心存感激。）

questions.stem: What did Steve Foran and his team do in the experiment?
options: They induced strangers to talk with them.
They helped 15 to 20 people in a bad mood.
They held doors open for people at various places.
They interviewed people who didn't say thank you.
optionsZh: 他们引导陌生人与他们交谈。
他们帮助了15到20个心情不好的人。
他们在不同地点为人们扶门。
他们采访了没有说谢谢的人。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：They held doors open for people at various places.（他们在不同地点为人们扶门。）

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report?
options: People can be educated to be grateful.
Most people express gratitude for help.
Most people have bad days now and then.
People are ungrateful when in a bad mood.
optionsZh: 人们可以被教育得懂感恩。
大多数人会对帮助表达感激。
大多数人时不时会有糟糕的日子。
人们在心情不好时不懂感恩。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Most people express gratitude for help.（大多数人会对帮助表达感激。）

questions.stem: What is the man's purpose for calling the woman?
options: To order a solar panel installation.
To report a serious leak in his roof.
To enquire about solar panel installations.
To complain about the faulty solar panels.
optionsZh: 订购太阳能电池板安装服务。
报告他屋顶有严重漏水。
咨询太阳能电池板安装事宜。
投诉有问题的太阳能电池板。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：To enquire about solar panel installations.（咨询太阳能电池板安装事宜。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man's neighbor from the conversation?
options: He plans to install solar panels.
He owns a four-bedroom house.
He saves $300 a year.
He has a large family.
optionsZh: 他计划安装太阳能电池板。
他拥有一栋四居室房屋。
他每年节省300美元。
他有一个大家庭。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：He has a large family.（他有一个大家庭。）

questions.stem: What is one of the man's chief concerns?
options: The service of the solar panel company.
The cost of a solar panel installation.
The maintenance of the solar panels.
The quality of the solar panels.
optionsZh: 太阳能电池板公司的服务。
太阳能电池板安装的费用。
太阳能电池板的维护。
太阳能电池板的质量。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：The cost of a solar panel installation.（太阳能电池板安装的费用。）

questions.stem: How long will it take a typical household to make back the initial investment?
options: One year and a half.
Less than four years.
Roughly six years.
About five years.
optionsZh: 一年半。
不到四年。
大约六年。
大约五年。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：About five years.（大约五年。）

questions.stem: Where is the conversation taking place?
options: At a travel agency.
At an Australian airport.
At an airline transfer service.
At a local transportation authority.
optionsZh: 在旅行社。
在澳大利亚的机场。
在航空公司中转服务处。
在当地交通管理局。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：At a travel agency.（在旅行社。）

questions.stem: Why is the woman interested in package holidays?
options: She would be able to visit more scenic spots.
She wanted to save as much money as possible.
She would like to have everything taken care of.
She wanted to spend more time with her family.
optionsZh: 她能够游览更多景点。
她想尽可能多地省钱。
她希望一切都有人安排妥当。
她想和家人度过更多时间。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：She would like to have everything taken care of.（她希望一切都有人安排妥当。）

questions.stem: How long does the woman want to go for the holiday?
options: Four days.
Five days.
One week.
Two weeks.
optionsZh: 四天。
五天。
一周。
两周。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：Two weeks.（两周。）

questions.stem: What does the woman say she likes about the holiday package?
options: Choosing some activities herself.
Spending Christmas with Australians.
Driving along the Great Ocean Road.
Learning more about wine making.
optionsZh: 自己选择一些活动。
与澳大利亚人一起过圣诞节。
沿着大洋路自驾。
更多地了解葡萄酒酿造。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Choosing some activities herself.（自己选择一些活动。）

questions.stem: What would tourists have to do when they visit Indonesia's Bali Island?
options: Bring their own bags when shopping.
Use public transport when traveling.
Dispose of their trash properly.
Pay a green tax upon arrival.
optionsZh: 购物时自带购物袋。
旅行时使用公共交通。
妥善处理自己的垃圾。
抵达时缴纳绿色税。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：Pay a green tax upon arrival.（抵达时缴纳绿色税。）

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Indonesia?
options: It has not been doing a good job in recycling.
It has witnessed a rise in accidental drowning.
It has not attracted many tourists in recent years.
It has experienced an overall decline in air quality.
optionsZh: 它在回收利用方面做得不好。
它目睹了意外溺水事件的增加。
近年来它没有吸引很多游客。
它经历了空气质量的整体下降。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：It has not been doing a good job in recycling.（它在回收利用方面做得不好。）

questions.stem: What is the new plan Governor Koster recently announced?
options: To charge a small fee on plastic products in supermarkets.
To ban single-use plastic bags and straws on Bali Island.
To promote the use of paper bags for shopping.
To impose a penalty on anyone caught littering.
optionsZh: 对超市里的塑料产品收取小额费用。
禁止在巴厘岛使用一次性塑料袋和吸管。
推广使用纸袋购物。
对任何被抓到乱扔垃圾的人处以罚款。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：To ban single-use plastic bags and straws on Bali Island.（禁止在巴厘岛使用一次性塑料袋和吸管。）

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about the North Atlantic right whale?
options: It gives birth to several babies at a time.
It is the least protected mammal species.
It's breeding grounds are now better preserved.
It's population is now showing signs of increase.
optionsZh: 它一次产下几头幼崽。
它是受保护程度最低的哺乳动物物种。
它的繁殖地现在得到了更好的保护。
它的种群数量现在显示出增长的迹象。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：It's population is now showing signs of increase.（它的种群数量现在显示出增长的迹象。）

questions.stem: What has caused the decline of the whale population in recent years?
options: Global warming.
Polluted seawaters.
Commercial hunting.
Decreasing birthrates.
optionsZh: 全球变暖。
海水污染。
商业捕猎。
出生率下降。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Commercial hunting.（商业捕猎。）

questions.stem: Why do the whales travel to the Northeast Coast of America in the early spring?
options: To mate.
To look for food.
To escape hunters.
To seek breeding grounds.
optionsZh: 交配。
寻找食物。
逃避捕猎者。
寻找繁殖地。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：To look for food.（寻找食物。）

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Americans?
options: They prefer to drink low-fat milk.
They think milk is good for health.
They consume less milk these days.
They buy more milk than the British.
optionsZh: 他们更喜欢喝低脂牛奶。
他们认为牛奶有益健康。
他们如今消耗的牛奶更少了。
他们购买的牛奶比英国人多。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：They consume less milk these days.（他们如今消耗的牛奶更少了。）

questions.stem: How do Americans and British people think of milk nowadays?
options: It is not as healthy as once thought.
It is not easy to stay fresh for long.
It benefits the elderly more.
It tends to make people fat.
optionsZh: 它不像曾经认为的那样健康。
它不容易长时间保持新鲜。
它对老年人更有益。
它往往使人发胖。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：It is not as healthy as once thought.（它不像曾经认为的那样健康。）

questions.stem: Why does drinking milk cause pain in some people?
options: They drink too many pints every day.
They are sensitive to certain minerals.
They lack the necessary proteins to digest it.
They have eaten food incompatible with milk.
optionsZh: 他们每天喝太多品脱的牛奶。
他们对某些矿物质敏感。
他们缺乏消化牛奶所需的蛋白质。
他们吃了与牛奶不相容的食物。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：They lack the necessary proteins to digest it.（他们缺乏消化牛奶所需的蛋白质。）

questions.stem: What does the passage say is a benefit of milk?
options: It is easier for sick people to digest.
It provides some necessary nutrients.
It is healthier than other animal products.
It supplies the body with enough calories.
optionsZh: 病人更容易消化它。
它提供一些必需的营养素。
它比其他动物产品更健康。
它为身体提供足够的卡路里。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：It provides some necessary nutrients.（它提供一些必需的营养素。）

sections.title: 写作
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅰ · 30 分钟 · 120–180 词

items.prompt: For this part , you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on the topic Changes in the way of Transportation. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
items.rubric: CET 写作 15 分制：切题 3、表达 9、字数 3
items.sample:
How people travel has changed dramatically over the past few decades. In the past, most of my grandparents'
generation walked or rode bicycles to work, and a trip to another city took a whole day by slow train.
Nowadays, the picture looks completely different.
The most obvious change lies in the variety and speed of transport. Today we can take the subway across a
huge city in minutes, reach a distant province by high-speed rail in a few hours, or simply open an app to call a
car or unlock a shared bike. Two forces drive this shift. Technological progress makes fast and smart travel
possible, while rising incomes and growing environmental concerns push people toward high-speed rail and
new-energy vehicles.
In my view, these changes have made our lives far more convenient and our cities greener. As technology
keeps advancing, I firmly believe transportation will become even faster, cleaner and smarter in the years
to come.

items.stem: When my son completes a task, I can't help but praise him. It's only natural to give praise where praise is due, right? But is there such a thing as too much praise? According to psychologist Katherine Phillip, children don't benefit from {{1}} praise as much as we'd like to think. "Parents often praise, believing they are building their child's self-confidence. However, over-praising can have a {{2}} effect," says Phillip. "When we use the same praise {{3}} , it may become empty and no longer valued by the child. It can also become an expectation that anything they do must be {{4}} with praise. This may lead to the child avoiding taking risks due to fear of {{5}} their parents." Does this mean we should do away with all the praise? Phillip says no. "The key to healthy praise is to focus on the process rather than the {{6}} . It is the recognition of a child's attempt, or the process in which they achieved something, that is essential," she says. "Parents should encourage their child to take the risks needed to learn and grow." So how do we break the {{7}} of praise we're all so accustomed to? Phillip says it's important to {{8}} between "person praise" and "process praise". "Person praise is {{9}} saying how great someone is. It's a form of personal approval. Process praise is acknowledgement of the efforts the person has just {{10}} . Children who receive person praise are more likely to feel shame after losing," says Phillip.
options: choose
constant
disappointing
distinguish
exhausting
experienced
negative
outcome
pattern
plural
repeatedly
rewarded
separately
simply
undertaken

【定位】According to psychologist Katherine Phillip, children don't benefit from ____ praise as much as we'd like to think.
【依据】答案是 constant：填回后与所在句 according、psychologist、katherine、phillip、children、don't 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】However, over-praising can have a ____ effect," says Phillip.
【依据】答案是 negative：填回后与所在句 however、over-praising、effect、says、phillip 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】"When we use the same praise ____ , it may become empty and no longer valued by the child.
【依据】答案是 repeatedly：填回后与所在句 when、use、same、praise、become、empty 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】It can also become an expectation that anything they do must be ____ with praise.
【依据】答案是 rewarded：填回后与所在句 become、expectation、anything、praise 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】This may lead to the child avoiding taking risks due to fear of ____ their parents." Does this mean we should do away with all the praise?
【依据】答案是 disappointing：填回后与所在句 lead、child、avoiding、taking、risks、due 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】"The key to healthy praise is to focus on the process rather than the ____ .
【依据】答案是 outcome：填回后与所在句 key、healthy、praise、focus、process、rather 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】"Parents should encourage their child to take the risks needed to learn and grow." So how do we break the ____ of praise we're all so accustomed to?
【依据】答案是 pattern：填回后与所在句 parents、encourage、child、take、risks、needed 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Phillip says it's important to ____ between "person praise" and "process praise".
【依据】答案是 distinguish：填回后与所在句 phillip、says、it's、important、between、person 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】"Person praise is ____ saying how great someone is.
【依据】答案是 simply：填回后与所在句 person、praise、saying、how、great、someone 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Process praise is acknowledgement of the efforts the person has just ____ .
【依据】答案是 undertaken：填回后与所在句 process、praise、acknowledgement、efforts、person、just 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

sections.title: 长篇阅读匹配
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅲ Section B · 10 句匹配段落

paragraphs.text: Too often still, we think we know what poverty looks like. It's the way we've been taught, the images we've been force-fed for decades. The chronically homeless. The undocumented immigrant. The urban poor, usually personified as a woman of color, the "welfare queen" politicians still too often reference.

But as income inequality rises to record levels in the United States, even in the midst of a record economic expansion, those familiar images are outdated, hurtful, and counterproductive to focusing attention on solutions and building ladders of opportunity.

Today's faces of income inequality and lack of opportunity look like all of us. It's Anna Landre, a disabled Georgetown University student fighting to keep health benefits that allow her the freedom to live her life. It's Tiffanie Standard, a counselor for young women of color in Philadelphia who want to be tech entrepreneurs—but who must work multiple jobs to stay afloat. It's Ken Outlaw, a welder in rural North Carolina whose dream of going back to school at a local community college was dashed by Hurricane Florence—just one of the extreme weather events that have tipped the balance for struggling Americans across the nation.

If these are the central characters of our story about poverty, what layers of perceptions, myths, and realities must we unearth to find meaningful solutions and support? In pursuit of revealing this complicated reality, Mothering Justice, led by women of color, went last year to the state capital in Lansing, Michigan, to lobby on issues that affect working mothers. One of the Mothering Justice organizers went to the office of a state representative to talk about the lack of affordable childcare—the vestiges(痕迹) of a system that expected mothers to stay home with their children while their husbands worked. A legislative staffer dismissed the activist's concerns, telling her "my husband took care of that—I stayed home."

That comment, says Mothering Justice director Danielle Atkinson, "was meant to shame" and relied on the familiar notion that a woman of color concerned about income inequality and programs that promote mobility must by definition be a single mom, probably with multiple kids. In this case, the Mothering Justice activist happened to be married. And in most cases in the America of 2019, the images that come to mind when we hear the words poverty or income inequality fail miserably in reflecting a complicated reality: poverty touches virtually all of us. The face of income inequality, for all but a very few of us, is the one we each see in the mirror.

How many of us are poor in the U.S.? It depends on who you ask. According to the Census Bureau, 38 million people in the U.S. are living below the official poverty thresholds. Taking into account economic need beyond that absolute measure, the Institute for Policy Studies found that 140 million people are poor or low-income. That's almost half the U.S. population.

Whatever the measure, within that massive group, poverty is extremely diverse. We know that some people are more affected than others, like children, the elderly, people with disabilities, and people of color.

But the fact that 4 in 10 Americans can't come up with $400 in an emergency is a commonly cited statistic for good reason: economic instability stretches across race, gender, and geography. It even reaches into the middle classes, as real wages have stagnated(不增长) for all but the very wealthy and temporary spells of financial instability are not uncommon.

Negative images remain of who is living in poverty as well as what is needed to move out of it. The big American myth is that you can pull yourself up by your own efforts and change a bad situation into a good one. The reality is that finding opportunity without help from families, friends, schools, and community is virtually impossible. And the playing field is nothing close to level.

The FrameWorks Institute, a research group that focuses on public framing of issues, has studied what sustains stereotypes and narratives of poverty in the United Kingdom. "People view economic success and wellbeing in life as a product of choice, willpower, and drive," says Nat Kendall-Taylor, CEO of FrameWorks. "When we see people who are struggling," he says, those assumptions "lead us to the perception that people in poverty are lazy, they don't care, and they haven't made the right decisions."

Does this sound familiar? Similar ideas surround poverty in the U.S. And these assumptions give a false picture of reality. "When people enter into that pattern of thinking," says Kendall-Taylor, "it's cognitively comfortable to make sense of issues of poverty in that way. It creates a kind of cognitive blindness—all of the factors external to a person's drive and choices that they've made become invisible and fade from view."

Those external factors include the difficulties accompanying low-wage work or structural discrimination based on race, gender, or ability. Assumptions get worse when people who are poor use government benefits to help them survive. There is a great tension between "the poor" and those who are receiving what has become a dirty word: "welfare."

According to the General Social Survey, 71 percent of respondents believe the country is spending too little on "assistance to the poor". On the other hand, 22 percent think we are spending too little on "welfare": 37 percent believe we are spending too much.

"Poverty has been interchangeable with people of color—specifically black women and black mothers," says Atkinson of Mothering Justice. It's true that black mothers are more affected by poverty than many other groups, yet they are disproportionately the face of poverty. For example, Americans routinely overestimate the share of black recipients of public assistance programs.

In reality, most people will experience some form of financial hardship at some point in their lives. Indeed, people tend to dip in and out of poverty, perhaps due to unexpected obstacles like losing a job, or when hours of a low-wage job fluctuate.
Something each of us can do is to treat each other with the dignity and sympathy that is deserved and to understand deeply that the issue of poverty touches all of us.

sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅲ Section C · 2 篇 × 5 题

items.passage: Boredom has, paradoxically, become quite interesting to academics lately. In early May, London's Boring Conference celebrated seven years of delighting in dullness. At this event, people flocked to talks about weather, traffic jams and vending-machine sounds, among other sleep-inducing topics. What, exactly, is everybody studying? One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity." But how can you quantify a person's boredom level and compare it with someone else's? In 1986, psychologists introduced the Boredom Proneness Scale, designed to measure an individual's overall tendency to feel bored. By contrast, the Multidimensional State Boredom Scale, developed in 2008, measures a person's feelings of boredom in a given situation. Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling. In fact, many of us would choose pain over boredom. One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self-administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes. Researching this phenomenon, another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films, during which they could self-administer electric shocks. The bored volunteers shocked themselves more and harder than the sad or neutral ones did. But boredom isn't all bad. By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity. An early study gave participants abundant time to complete problem-solving and word-association exercises. Once all the obvious answers were exhausted, participants gave more and more inventive answers to combat boredom. A British study took these findings one step further, asking subjects to complete a creative challenge (coming up with a list of alternative uses for a household item). One group of subjects did a boring activity first, while the others went straight to the creative task. Those whose boredom pumps had been primed were more productive. In our always-connected world, boredom may be a hard-to-define state, but it is a fertile one. Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while, and you might unlock your next big idea.

items.passage: Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why. South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost. But forests are also changing in rich Western countries. They are growing larger, both in the sense that they occupy more land and that the trees in them are bigger. What is going on? Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees. In 1990 28% of Spain was forested; now the proportion is 37%. In both Greece and Italy, the growth was from 26% to 32% over the same period. Forests are gradually taking more land in America and Australia. Perhaps most astonishing is the trend in Ireland. Roughly 1% of that country was forested when it became independent in 1922. Now forests cover 11% of the land, and the government wants to push the proportion to 18% by the 2040s. Two things are fertilising this growth. The first is the abandonment of farmland, especially in high, dry places where nothing grows terribly well. When farmers give up trying to earn a living from farming or herding, trees simply move in. The second is government policy and subsidy. Throughout history, governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building. Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air. The justifications change, the desire for more trees remains constant. The greening of the West does not delight everyone. Farmers complain that land is being taken out of use by generously subsidised tree plantations. Parts of Spain and Portugal suffer from terrible forest fires. Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows. They will have to get used to the trees, however. The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere.

items.zh: 春节前夕吃团圆饭是中国人的传统。团圆饭是一年中最重要的晚餐也是家庭团聚的最佳时机家人生活在不同地方的家庭尤其如此。团圆饭上的菜肴丰富多样其中有些菜肴有特殊含义。例如鱼是不可缺少的一道菜因为汉语中的"鱼"字和"余"字听上去一样。在中国的许多地方饺子也是一道重要的佳肴因为饺子象征着财富和好运。
items.reference: It is a tradition for Chinese people to have the reunion dinner on Chinese New Year's Eve The reunion dinner is the most important dinner of the year and also the best occasion for family reunion, especially for families whose members live in different places. The dishes served at the reunion dinner are rich and varied, some of which have special meanings. For example, fish is an indispensable dish, because the Chinese character for "fish" (yu) sounds the same as the character for "surplus" (yu). In many parts of China, dumplings are also an important dish, because they symbolize wealth and good luck.
